{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Fedora RPM build and review

on:
  push:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: fedora:44
      options: --privileged

    steps:
      - name: Install git
        run: dnf install -y git

      - name: Trust the GitHub Actions workspace
        run: git config --global --add safe.directory "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}"

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}

      - name: Cache DNF dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: /var/cache/dnf
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-dnf-${{ hashFiles('.github/workflows/fedora-rpm-build-review.yml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-dnf-

      - name: Install build dependencies
        run: dnf install -y fedora-packager python3-specfile

      - name: Run build script
        run: |
          cd rpm
          ./build.sh

      - name: Run review script
        run: |
          cd rpm
          ./review.sh

      - name: Upload Review Results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Fedora Review Report
          path: rpm/review-leilfs/review.txt",
  "rationale": "The workflow repeatedly downloads dependencies with dnf on every run (git, then fedora-packager/python3-specfile) with no dependency cache. Pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Cache dependency downloads) is evidence-supported: it targets repeated dependency fetching, keeps all installation and required tests, and reports a modest aggregate VM-time reduction. Adding an actions/cache@v4 step for /var/cache/dnf after checkout and before the build-dependency install reuses downloaded packages across runs. The cache key is keyed on the workflow file (which lists the packages) so dependency changes invalidate the cache, satisfying the lockfile/environment precondition as closely as possible for a dnf-based workflow. No build or test steps are removed, permissions are unchanged, and no new secrets, deployment operations, or privileged actions are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
